name: Lock in stasis
summary: Takes a target out of the fight altogether for a while: it can't move, fire or use abilities, and nothing can hurt or help it until the effect ends. Unlike a freeze, it sets up no bonus damage; the held target is shielded too, so the point is to isolate it, split a fight or buy time. Some versions hold one target, by a beam the caster must keep on it or by a timed prison; others catch everyone in an area, or wait as a hidden trap. In the harshest form the hold becomes an erasure: kept on long enough (longer for tougher targets) the target is removed outright, but it never wears down, and if the caster lets go or dies it comes back unharmed. Turned on a teammate, the same effect becomes a shelter from burst damage, at the cost of taking them out of the fight as well.
counterplay: Kill or interrupt the caster: a beam or channel ends the moment it does, and the target comes back unharmed.
Struggle out of a beam hold: the held player holds F to fill a break bar, and the beam snaps if the bar fills before the erase does.
Bring numbers: a single-target caster holds one enemy at a time, so the rest of the group can focus it down.
Out-range it or catch it with area fire while it stands still on its target.
Don't waste shots on a target in stasis; reposition around the spot where it will reappear instead.
Fly: the soldier-carried beam in the source unit can't reach aircraft, so a beam caster is exposed to air attack.
Spot hidden stasis traps with a detector or shoot them, and spread out so an area hold catches fewer of you.

other_examples.note: An area power: everything inside drops out of time for a while, unable to act or be damaged. Players use it to shelter their own troops and buildings from superweapons. Other units may move into the empty space, and are destroyed when the held objects return, which also hurts those objects badly.

A targeted area spell: whatever it catches can neither move, attack nor cast, and nothing can attack or cast on it. Players use it to split an attacking army so the rest can be beaten piece by piece, or to park the most dangerous enemies, such as siege tanks, while their escort is destroyed.

The caster leaves a cloaked ward on the ground; when enemies trip it, those in a small area are frozen for a long time. While trapped they can't be attacked, and their own side's abilities can't reach them either.

A single-target spell on a short cooldown that hides one unit, enemy or ally, for a few seconds: it is disabled and invulnerable, and the enemy version takes damage and loses part of its mana pool when the prison ends. An ally is imprisoned without the damage, so it works as a shelter; a later upgrade lets the sheltered ally keep walking slowly, untargetable but unable to act.

A long-range ultimate thrown at a spot after a short flight: every unit inside, friend or foe, turrets and large monsters included, is put in stasis for a couple of seconds, and the enemies it hits are stunned for the same time. It can save allies, stall a fight or freeze a turret, and a bad throw locks up your own team.

shooter_analogues.note: A cone wave in a third-person co-op shooter that pushes enemies and allies into a separate plane for a time. Weapons only work between combatants on the same plane, so a banished target is cut off from the fight rather than frozen; a banished player can roll to leave early, and a related ability freezes banished enemies in place.

player_translation.summary: Hold a beam on one enemy (or a teammate) to lift them out of the fight: while it holds, they can't act and nobody can hurt them. Let go, or get killed, and they drop back in unharmed. The harsh version erases a target that is held long enough, which counts as a kill.
as_user: You pick one target and take it out of the fight: the enemy tank that was winning is suddenly a statue nobody can touch, so your team fights the rest of theirs a player short.
In erase versions you commit: you stand still with the beam on, a bar fills more slowly for tougher targets, and if you are interrupted all that time is lost.

You can turn it on a teammate who is about to die, sheltering them from a burst or a bombardment; they lose their turn in the fight while you hold, and in erase versions you must let go before the bar fills.
You do no damage yourself, so your value is in timing: hold the right target at the right moment, and let your team handle what is left.
as_target: Your screen greys out and your unit is frozen in place inside a visible shell; you can still watch the fight and ping, but you can't move or fire.
A bar shows how long the hold has left, or how close an erase is; your team sees it too.

Against a beam you are not helpless: hold F, the universal shake-off, to struggle. A second bar fills while you struggle and the beam snaps when it is full, so an erase becomes a race between the two bars. Timed prisons and fields can't be shaken off, but they are short.
From a beam hold, your team can also free you at once, and unharmed, by killing or knocking out the caster.
When it ends you reappear where you were, so plan your first move while you wait.
teammates: Defenders get a clear rescue job: find and kill the caster, who is fragile and standing still.
Attackers use the hold to win a numbers fight: lock the enemy's biggest threat, then focus the rest.
Sheltering works across the team: a stasis user can save a carrier, a healer or the player holding the objective from a burst.
Both teams learn not to shoot a target in stasis, and to stand around the spot where it will return.
controls: Beam version: hold Q with the cursor on a target to keep the beam on; release to let go. If the beam is the unit's primary weapon, it sits on left mouse instead.
Timed version: press Q on a target under the cursor; the hold then runs on its own for a fixed time.
The same key works on teammates; aiming at an ally shows a shelter marker instead of an attack marker.
Trap and field variants: press Q to place the ward or throw the field at the spot under the cursor.
Target, with the universal keys: hold F to struggle against a beam hold, which fills a break bar; middle mouse pings the caster for your team.
feedback: A distinct stasis look, such as a clock-like shell or a desaturated, translucent body, clearly different from ice (which means freeze and shatter: shoot it) so players know shots are wasted.
A beam line from caster to target, readable from above, with a ring around the target that fills as the hold or erase timer runs.
Shots that hit a held target visibly pass through or flash off it, with a 'no effect' sound.
Kill feed entry for an erase, credited to the caster; a separate 'sheltered' icon when a teammate was saved.
On the minimap, held units show as hollow markers so both teams know who is out of the fight.
changes_from_rts: Being held is no fun for a player, so every hold needs a visible timer and a clear way out: struggling against a beam with hold F, or a teammate killing the caster. Timed versions stay short.
Erasing a player outright is too harsh at low tiers: keep the erase for T3 casters, make it slow against high-tier targets, and count it as a normal kill with respawn.
A target that leaves stasis gets a brief immunity to being held again, so two casters can't chain-lock one player.
Sheltering a teammate must not become free invulnerability for objective players: a held player can't capture, carry or contest objectives.

In Red Alert 2 the erase time is set by the beam's strength and the target's full health, never by its armour or the damage it has already taken; here tie it to the target's tier so prices still mean something.

In Red Alert 2 the legionnaire must keep firing to hold its target, and every move it makes is a teleport, so it stands still while it holds; here the caster may walk slowly while holding, so the hold stays playable, but it can't fire anything else until it lets go.

team_play.notes: A hold creates a short numbers advantage that attackers must cash in fast and defenders can break by killing the caster; sheltering lets a stasis user protect a teammate from burst. The caster stands still and fragile on its target, so it needs a bodyguard.

notes: Needs a stasis state that removes a unit from damage, targeting and collision but keeps it in place and visible, and every system (damage, healing, attachments, objectives, auras) must respect it.

The channelled version needs a beam with range and line-of-sight checks, an erase timer scaled by target tier, a struggle bar for the target, and clean break rules when the caster dies, moves out of range or is disabled.
Area and trap variants need hit tests for everyone in the area, friend and foe, and safe handling of anything standing where a held unit will reappear.
Networking: the server must decide when a hold starts and ends, so a target never takes damage in the frame stasis begins.
UI on both sides: held-player screen, hold and struggle bars, shelter markers and kill-feed credit.
It removes a player from play entirely, the most frustrating control effect there is; long holds or chain-locks make the target quit.
An erase that ignores armour lets a soldier delete the most expensive vehicle on the field; tier scaling and slow erases on big targets are essential.
Shelter on a teammate can be abused to dodge every burst or ultimate; it needs a cooldown and must block objective play.
Area holds that catch both sides can be used to stall objectives indefinitely.
From above, stasis can be confused with a freeze (which invites shots) or with plain invulnerability; it needs its own unmistakable look.
Players must see at a glance who is holding whom, which means a visible beam or tether, and whether the target is an enemy being erased or an ally being sheltered.
A unit returning from stasis appears suddenly; a short fade-in warning is needed so nobody is surprised by it.

variants.name: Hold to erase
variants.summary: Keep a beam on one target: it is frozen and untouchable while the beam holds, and erased once a bar fills, more slowly for tougher targets. Let go or die and it returns unharmed, with no damage carried over.

variants.name: Timed prison
variants.summary: A targeted shot locks one enemy or teammate away for a short fixed time; there is no erase, and the target returns where it was when the time runs out.

adds_weaknesses.why: Holds one target for a short fixed time and does no damage while it lasts: nobody can hurt the held enemy either, and it comes back where it was when the time is up.

countered_by.why: Long-range fire hits the caster from beyond the reach of its prison shot, and only one target at a time is ever locked away.
Locked out of its abilities, it can't cast the prison at all.

variants.name: Shelter a teammate
variants.summary: Only friendly targets: lift a teammate out of the fight to save them from a burst or a bombardment, at the cost of their turn in the fight and, in erase versions, the risk of holding too long.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 Chrono Legionnaire force-firing on friends; Dota 2 Astral Imprisonment on allies; Red Alert 3 Chrono Rift against superweapons

adds_strengths.why: Can save a teammate from a killing burst by lifting them clear of the fight for a moment.

adds_weaknesses.why: It does nothing to enemies, and a sheltered teammate can't fight or hold an objective while it lasts.

variants.name: Stasis field
variants.summary: An area version thrown at a spot: everything inside, friend and foe, is held for a short time, splitting one fight into two.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft Arbiter Stasis Field, Red Alert 3 Chrono Rift, League of Legends Bard's Tempered Fate

adds_strengths.why: Removes everyone in an area from the fight for a short time, however big or well armoured, splitting the enemy into two smaller fights; it can also shelter teammates caught under a bombardment.

adds_weaknesses.why: Holds friend and foe alike, does no damage, and a badly placed field locks up its own team.

countered_by.why: Units that fight from far back are rarely inside the field and keep firing while the front is held, and a spread-out team loses only a few players to it.

variants.name: Stasis trap
variants.summary: Place a hidden ward that holds the first enemies to walk into it for a long time; nobody can hurt them while they are held, so the team uses the time to reposition or take ground.

adds_strengths.why: Works while the caster is elsewhere: the first enemies over a hidden ward are taken out of the fight.

adds_weaknesses.why: A ward sits still until enemies walk into it, and detectors or a careful player find and destroy it.

countered_by.why: A detector reveals the hidden ward, so it can be shot or walked around before it springs.

variants.name: Crushing return
variants.summary: While held units are out of time their space is empty; anything standing there when they return is destroyed, and the returning units are badly hurt too.

adds_weaknesses.why: Holds one target at a time, and its return badly hurts whatever it held, a sheltered teammate included, and destroys anything standing in its place, friend or foe.

variants.name: Shift to another plane
variants.summary: Instead of freezing, the target is pushed into a separate layer of the battlefield for a time: it can still move, but can only hurt or be hurt by others in the same layer, and a teammate of the caster can step in to finish it.
variants.seen_in: Warframe Limbo's Banish and Rift plane

adds_weaknesses.why: Does no damage itself, and the target is only cut off, not helpless: it can still move and fight anyone who follows it into the other layer.

adds_strengths.why: Takes any one enemy out of the fight while it holds, however big or well armoured, and can shelter a teammate the same way.

adds_weaknesses.why: Holds one target at a time and deals no damage: nobody can hurt the held enemy either, and if the caster stops or dies it returns unharmed.

counters.why: Armour makes no difference: the heaviest tank is held out of the fight as surely as a soldier.

countered_by.why: Area fire catches the caster while it is busy with one target, and a group can't all be held at once.
Long-range fire kills the caster from beyond its reach while it holds a target, and the target returns unharmed.

open_questions: Should erasing a player be possible at all, or should every hold end with the target returning? (Recommended: erase only for T3 casters, slow against high-tier targets, counted as a normal kill.)

How fast should struggling (hold F) break a beam hold, compared with the erase time? (Recommended: faster than any erase of a target of the caster's tier or higher, so erases land only on cheaper targets or with help.)
Should sheltering teammates be part of the base pattern, as in Red Alert 2 and Dota 2, or only a variant?
Can a held unit be pushed, pulled or carried by other effects, or is it fixed in place?

shooter_fit.reason: A dramatic one-on-one moment with a clear rescue (kill the caster), and MOBAs show single-target holds work for player heroes; but removing a player from play is harsh, so it needs short timers, visible bars and strict tier rules.

review.notes: Re-checked field by field against its sources by the batch r1 checker, which covered all 33 batch patterns; research/r1/checker/checks.json lists every field and verdict. Nothing was found wrong.
